judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1200. It would have legalized cannabis for adults 21 and over, who could buy, carry, use and share small amounts. Sales would run through state-run stores under the Liquor Control Board, the agency that runs state liquor stores, rather than private shops. Past cannabis convictions would be found in court records and cleared, and licenses would favor applicants from communities most affected by past drug enforcement. Carrying more than the personal limit would still bring fines, and growing without a permit would still be a crime. For someone under 21, possession would become a fine and a diversion program instead of a criminal record. The Pennsylvania House passed it 102-101. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 49. It would have created a Cannabis Control Board, and a fund to pay for it, and moved permits and the dispensing of cannabis to patients and caregivers under that board. It did not legalize recreational cannabis. It restructured the regulator for the existing medical marijuana program. The measure failed in the Pennsylvania Senate 23-27.
